about: Every feature of Freally OS, one tagged spec each, driven over CDP by tools/cdp-runner. A feature without a spec, or a spec without a feature, fails the run.

features.what: The bootloader verifies the signed image and paints Freally OS vX.Y.Z in Noto Sans: the whole screen, pixel for pixel.
One flipped bit in the image gets the integrity screen, with the reason, and nothing from the image runs.
A release bootloader boots its staging-signed release image.
A release bootloader refuses a dev-signed image: a key this computer doesn't trust.
Boot services exit, the runtime services move to the direct map, and Freally Core is entered with a BootInfo it accepts, then paints its screen.
A kernel fault stops on the panic screen in Noto, naming the exception, its RIP and the machine state, drawn exactly as the kernel logs it.
A kernel panic survives a warm reboot: the next boot finds the last-panic page, files it as a fault report from freally-core, and logs it once.
Freally Core starts conductor from the image as PID 1, its ELF re-checked and loaded W^X; conductor says it started and C0 is stamped.
The logger keeps every service's lines and the kernel's own, mirrors services' lines to COM1 in dev and e2e, and reads them back page by page.
Conductor starts services from their manifests; each one that restarts is killed in turn and is back within 200 ms.
devmgr reads the firmware's ACPI tables and finds every PCI function through MCFG's configuration space: exactly QEMU's own list.
drv-gop-fb offers the firmware's framebuffer as a write-combining VMO; filled with the UI kit's ground, the screen is that colour, every pixel.
Every printable character and modifier typed reaches drv-i8042 through IRQ 1 as scan code set 2 and comes out as the right Freally key code and US character.
The PS/2 mouse, found with its IntelliMouse wheel, reports through IRQ 12 every movement on both axes, each of its three buttons, and the wheel both ways, in HID's directions.
On a machine with no PS/2 controller, drv-i8042 says No PS/2 controller found. and ends cleanly: never restarted, nothing else disturbed.
Bytes through COM3 and back without losing one, while the door stalls so the driver must hold the line: 256 KB each run, 10 MB with --slow.
A command sent the moment the VM restarts, before the serial driver or the door exists, is still answered: nothing that arrives before a client opens the port is lost.
Every boot stage from B0 to S2 is stamped, in order, and conductor says them in one line; the firmware's own FPDT times are shown apart, or their absence said.
Slot B on trial with an image that crashes before conductor: three trial boots, then the fourth lands on slot A, and the log says the update didn't start.
Slot B on trial with a good image: it boots with a try spent, and conductor marks it Good through UEFI SetVariable 10 s after every boot service is running.
